description: Curated catalogue of legitimate, browser-playable games. Every entry was verified against its official page in September 2026.

fields.popularity: 1–3, editorial estimate based on public attention; not a measured statistic

games.description: The viral tile-sliding number puzzle. Merge matching tiles and chase the elusive 2048 tile.
games.details: Created in a single weekend in 2014 and released as open source under MIT. The official page is still maintained by the original author and works offline after first load.

games.name: Hextris
games.description: A fast-paced puzzle game inspired by Tetris, played on a spinning hexagon instead of a well.
games.details: Built by four students in 2015 and open sourced under GPL. It runs at full speed on almost any device, including phones.
games.developer: Logan Engstrom, Garrett Finucane, Noah Moroze, Michael Yang

games.name: Clumsy Bird
games.description: An open-source Flappy-Bird-style arcade game built with the MelonJS engine and hosted on GitHub Pages.
games.details: A well-known open-source demo of the MelonJS framework — tap or click to flap past the pipes.

games.name: Astray
games.description: A WebGL marble maze with realistic physics — roll the ball through procedurally generated corridors.
games.details: A classic WebGL demo by Rye Terrell using three.js and a physics engine; the maze is different every time.

games.name: HexGL
games.description: A futuristic anti-gravity racing game in the spirit of Wipeout, rendered in real-time WebGL.
games.details: Built by Thibaut Despoulain with three.js and released under MIT. Includes quality presets down to a mobile mode, though it plays best with a keyboard.

games.name: Underrun
games.description: A stylish WebGL twin-stick roguelite shooter about restoring a corrupted network, one node at a time.
games.details: Written in tiny, dependency-free JavaScript by Dominic Szablewski (PhobosLab) with a crisp neon aesthetic. The full source code is on GitHub.

games.name: Xibalba
games.description: A fast, chunky retro FPS with five levels, secrets and big guns — pure WebGL, no plugins.
games.details: Another PhobosLab engine showcase: an entire first-person shooter in a few hundred kilobytes of code, with an open-source repository.

games.name: QWOP
games.description: You are Qwop, the small nation's sole Olympic hopeful. Run 100 meters using only Q, W, O and P.
games.details: Bennett Foddy's infamously difficult ragdoll sprint from 2008, still hosted on the designer's own site.

games.name: Wordle
games.description: Guess the five-letter word in six tries. One new puzzle for everyone, every day.
games.details: Originally created by Josh Wardle in 2021 and acquired by The New York Times in 2022, where it runs free of charge. An account is only needed to sync stats across devices.
games.developer: The New York Times (orig. Josh Wardle)
games.freeNote: Free, no subscription needed for the daily puzzle.

games.name: Connections
games.description: Group sixteen words into four hidden categories without making four mistakes.
games.details: The New York Times' word-logic hit. Free daily puzzle; subscription only unlocks the archive.
games.freeNote: Daily puzzle free; archive requires a NYT Games subscription.

games.name: Semantle
games.description: Guess the secret word by meaning, not spelling — every guess is scored by semantic similarity.
games.details: Created by David Turner using word2vec embeddings, now part of The Word Finder. Unlimited guesses, hints available, and a full archive of past puzzles.

games.name: Contexto
games.description: Find the secret word using an AI that ranks every guess by how close it is in meaning.
games.details: One of the most popular post-Wordle word games: thousands of ranked guesses, unlimited attempts, daily puzzle.

games.name: Infinite Craft
games.description: Start with four elements and combine them into… literally anything, powered by live AI models.
games.details: Neal Agarwal's 2024 viral sandbox lets you discover absurd combinations — the crafting tree keeps growing forever. Requires an internet connection (combinations are generated server-side).

games.name: The Password Game
games.description: Create a password. It must contain a number, an emoji, today's Wordle answer, the moon phase…
games.details: Neal Agarwal's rule-stacking torture device that escalates from reasonable to unhinged. Wildly popular in 2023.

games.name: Little Alchemy 2
games.description: Mix the four classical elements to discover over 700 items in the official browser version.
games.details: Recloak's charming crafting encyclopedia — start with air, earth, fire and water and end up with philosophy and dinosaurs.

games.name: Universal Paperclips
games.description: You are a sentient AI whose only goal is to make paperclips. What could possibly go wrong?
games.details: Frank Lantz's legendary 2017 idle game about an AI apocalypse, still free to play in the browser. Trust us: play it blind.

games.name: A Dark Room
games.description: A minimalist text adventure that starts with a fire and ends… somewhere very different.
games.details: Doublespeak Games' cult classic incremental. The official web version is open source; a free mobile app also exists.

games.name: Game about Squares
games.description: Push squares onto matching dots. Sounds easy — 35 levels of escalating logic say otherwise.
games.details: A beautifully minimal indie puzzle by Andrey Shevchuk that became a cult favorite. Runs in any browser.

games.name: Powder Game
games.description: The legendary falling-sand physics playground: pour water, ignite gunpowder, grow forests.
games.details: ha55ii's Powder Game has run on DAN-BALL since 2006 and is still updated (ver 9.8). Playing is free with no account; uploading creations requires free site registration.
games.freeNote: Free to play; free site account needed only to save/upload creations.

games.name: Sandspiel
games.description: A modern falling-sand toy with pixels, gases, plants and lightning — all simulated on the GPU.
games.details: Max Bittker's WebGL remake of the powder-game genre, open source on GitHub, with a built-in community gallery of creations.

games.name: Cookie Clicker
games.description: The game that launched a thousand idle games. Click a cookie. Bake the universe.
games.details: Julien 'Orteil' Thiennot's 2013 behemoth is still updated with new content years later, complete with a lore-heavy grandmapocalypse.

games.name: Kittens Game
games.description: A 'Dark Souls of incremental gaming': lead a village of kittens from catnip farming to space.
games.details: bloodrizer's deep civilization idle runs entirely in the browser and saves locally. An optional free account syncs progress across devices.
games.freeNote: Free; optional account for cross-device saves.

games.name: Trimps
games.description: A deceptively deep idle/strategy hybrid: breed workers, conquer zones, prestige forever.
games.details: An open-source incremental that has been continuously updated for a decade. Runs from its GitHub Pages site with no account.

games.name: Evolve
games.description: Grow a species from the stone age through interstellar colonization in this incremental epic.
games.details: A free, open-source idle game with enormous depth — magic, space, arpa projects and more. Saves locally in your browser.

games.name: Melvor Idle
games.description: A feature-rich idle adventure inspired by RuneScape skill training — 25+ skills, all in the browser.
games.details: The core web version is free; optional paid expansions and a mobile app exist. Progress can be saved locally or synced with a free account.
games.freeNote: Core game free; optional paid expansions.

games.name: Krunker
games.description: The pixel-art arena FPS that defined browser shooters — movement, custom maps and trading.
games.details: Created by Sidney de Vries and now operated by FRVR. Still online and playable with an active custom-games community, though the player base has declined significantly since its 2019–2021 peak.
games.notes: Still online; reduced player base since FRVR acquisition (2023).

games.name: Shell Shockers
games.description: A first-person shooter where everyone is an egg. Crack the competition in 6v6 team battles.
games.details: Built by Blue Wizard Digital (founded by ex-PopCap co-founder Jason Kapalka) with the official site at shellshock.io. Free, with cosmetic-only purchases.

games.name: Venge.io
games.description: A polished 3D arena shooter with heroes, abilities and a huge library of community maps.
games.details: An independent browser FPS with 1,000+ community maps, clans and customization. Free to play with cosmetic items.

games.name: Smash Karts
games.description: Bumper-kart battles with rockets, grenades and machine guns. Instant mayhem in 3D arenas.
games.details: Tall Team's kart arena game has become one of the most-played 3D io games. Free, with cosmetic-only purchases.

games.name: Zombs Royale
games.description: A 100-player 2D battle royale: drop in, loot up, outlive everyone else.
games.details: Originally by End Game and still going strong today with solo, duo and squad modes. Free with cosmetic purchases.
games.developer: End Game (operated by Lol Analytics LLC)

games.name: MooMoo.io
games.description: Gather resources, build a village and defend your windmills from everyone else on the server.
games.details: Sidney de Vries' base-building survival io game, now operated by FRVR. Note: the site sits behind a Cloudflare check, which some networks block.

games.name: Slither.io
games.description: The game that ate 2016: grow the longest snake in a pit of thousands of players.
games.details: Steve Howse's phenomenon remains one of the most recognizable browser games ever made. Play as a guest instantly.
games.freeNote: Free with ads and optional cosmetics.

games.name: Agar.io
games.description: Eat cells smaller than you, dodge the ones bigger than you. The original io breakout hit.
games.details: Matheus Valadares' 2015 creation, now operated by Miniclip. Note that Miniclip retired its wider web-games portal in 2022 — Agar.io is one of the few survivors.
games.freeNote: Free with ads and optional cosmetics.

games.name: Diep.io
games.description: Shoot shapes, level up your tank and pick a class in the original tank-battle arena.
games.details: Matheus Valadares followed up Agar.io with this tank shooter; it still hosts full servers today.

games.name: Territorial.io
games.description: Expand your nation pixel by pixel across real-world maps against hundreds of players.
games.details: David Tschacher's real-time grand strategy io game supports 500+ players per match. The site uses a Cloudflare verification page on load.

games.name: Generals.io
games.description: Fast-paced real-time strategy: find the enemy general before they find yours.
games.details: Still actively updated (v31.x) with 1v1 seasons, custom maps and tournaments. Pick a username and play instantly.

games.name: OpenFront
games.description: An open-source territorial RTS: build cities, forge alliances, launch nukes — in the browser.
games.details: A community-driven fork lineage of WarFront.io inspired by Territorial.io, with ranked matchmaking and a public source code repository. Free with optional cosmetics; no account needed for solo play.
games.freeNote: Free with optional cosmetics; any purchase removes ads for life.

games.name: Bonk.io
games.description: Custom-physics sumo: shove everyone off the map and be the last ball standing.
games.details: Play instantly as a guest, or register to level up and build maps. Millions of community-made levels are one click away.

games.name: Starblast.io
games.description: Mine asteroids, upgrade your ship through 8 tiers and fight a galaxy of real players.
games.details: Neuronality's space shooter MMO with team mode, survival and an in-game level editor. Runs on any modern browser.

games.name: Deeeep.io
games.description: Start as a tiny fish and evolve up the ocean food chain — if something bigger doesn't eat you first.
games.details: Federico Mouse's evolution survival game with 30+ animal tiers, biome mechanics and pearl-defense team mode.

games.name: TETR.IO
games.description: A free, modern multiplayer stacker with ranked Tetra League, custom rooms and wild game modes.
games.details: osk's fan-made online stacker is the competitive scene's tool of choice. Browser client plus an optional desktop app. Free with cosmetic supporter perks.

games.name: Jstris
games.description: A lean, fast online stacker with live multiplayer, cheese races and 40-line sprints.
games.details: Play as a guest in one click. Popular with speedrunners for its precise handling and custom rulesets.

games.name: TagPro
games.description: Roll your ball into 4v4 capture-the-flag chaos — no login required, one keypress to play.
games.details: A community-run classic since 2013 with leagues (MLTP season 40 is running) and weekly games. Servers in NA, EU and AU.

games.name: Curve Fever Pro
games.description: The legendary 'snake on paper' party game: trap friends with your trail, grab power-ups, survive.
games.details: Hidden Monster Games' modern take on the Achtung die Kurve formula. Pick a username to play; account optional.

games.name: Skribbl.io
games.description: Draw, guess and laugh: the free drawing-and-guessing party game with custom rooms.
games.details: One of the most popular browser party games ever — create a private room for friends in seconds, fully free with no account.

games.name: Gartic Phone
games.description: The 'telephone game' with drawings: one prompt becomes increasingly unhinged art by the last player.
games.details: Onrizon's party hit supports large lobbies and many game modes. Free with cosmetic extras; no account required.

games.name: Codenames
games.description: The official online version of the hit word game — spymasters give one-word clues, teams guess.
games.details: Czech Games Edition's own free adaptation with online rooms and a video-call friendly design. No account needed.

games.name: Colonist.io
games.description: A polished free Catan-style settler game — trade, build and race for 10 victory points.
games.details: Play casual games instantly as a guest (thousands of matches run daily); a free account unlocks ranked play. The #1 free Settlers alternative on the web.

games.name: Lichess
games.description: The free, open-source, ad-free chess server: play, train, puzzle and watch — forever free.
games.details: Run by a nonprofit, Lichess is arguably the best chess experience on the internet at any price. Accounts are optional; anonymous play is fully supported.

games.name: Chess.com
games.description: The world's largest chess community: play online, solve puzzles and follow grandmaster streams.
games.details: Free tier covers unlimited daily games and puzzles; a paid membership adds lessons and deeper analysis. Account required to play.
games.freeNote: Freemium: unlimited free play; paid tier for extras.

games.name: Monkeytype
games.description: A beautiful, minimal typing test with 40+ modes, live stats and a huge language selection.
games.details: Open source and highly customizable — from zen mode to custom text. Saves your PBs locally with no account.

games.name: TypeRacer
games.description: Race real people (and literary characters) by typing famous passages as fast as you can.
games.details: The original multiplayer typing race. Play instantly as a guest; an account tracks history and WPM.

games.name: ZType
games.description: A typing game where your keyboard is a weapons system: type words to shoot down incoming ships.
games.details: PhobosLab's slick canvas shooter that secretly makes you a faster typist. One of the all-time great browser toys.

games.name: Quick, Draw!
games.description: Can a neural network recognize your doodle in 20 seconds? Six sketches, six guesses.
games.details: Google Creative Lab's playful AI experiment has been running since 2016. Free, no account, works with touch.

games.name: Minecraft Classic
games.description: Mojang's free browser edition of the original 2009 Minecraft — mine, build, repeat.
games.details: Released for the game's 10th anniversary and still online. Limited old-school blocks and 32-block build height; no account required.

games.name: Line Rider
games.description: Draw a line, ride it. The physics toy that spawned two decades of mesmerizing tracks.
games.details: The modern official web version, maintained as an open-source project with Boštjan Čadež's blessing. Includes track sharing and tools.

games.name: Slow Roads
games.description: An endless, procedurally generated driving meditation. No score, no timer — just the road.
games.details: Actively developed by an independent developer (updated through 2026) with vehicles, seasons, autodrive and full controller support. Free, no account.

games.name: GeoGuessr
games.description: Guess where in the world you are from a random Street View. The ultimate geography duel.
games.details: Now a freemium service: the free tier is one 5-round Daily Challenge per day and requires a free account; unlimited play, multiplayer and custom maps need a Pro subscription.
games.freeNote: Freemium: one free daily challenge (5 rounds, account required); Pro subscription for unlimited play.

games.name: Fallen London
games.description: A decade-deep gothic text world beneath a Victorian city. Choices, consequences, exquisite prose.
games.details: Failbetter Games' flagship narrative game is free to play with an account (needed to save your character). Enormous amounts of story.
games.freeNote: Free to play with optional paid story content.

games.name: Kingdom of Loathing
games.description: The stick-figure MMO that's been absurdly funny and free since 2003 — still updated today.
games.details: Asymmetric's comedy RPG runs on nearly any device with a browser. Creating a (free) character is required; the August 2026 announcements show it's actively maintained.
games.freeNote: Free; optional donations and Mr. Store items.

games.name: Subway Surfers
games.description: The 1.8-billion-download endless runner, officially playable in the browser on Poki.
games.details: SYBO Games' flagship has run on Poki since 2019 as the official web version (1.7 billion plays) with desktop, phone and tablet support. Free, no account.
games.source: Official Poki page (by SYBO) + PocketGamer.biz report

games.name: Retro Bowl
games.description: Retro-styled American football management with a surprisingly gripping passing game.
games.details: New Star Games' hit runs officially in the browser on Poki. Manage your roster, keep the fans happy, win the Retro Bowl. Free, no account.
games.developer: New Star Games (web version on Poki)
games.source: Official Poki page (by New Star Games)

games.name: Papa's Freezeria
games.description: Run the town's only milkshake shop: take orders, blend sundaes, chase perfect scores.
games.details: Flipline Studios hosts the entire Papa's series free on their official site in HTML5 — this is the classic 2011 Freezeria, remastered for modern browsers.

games.name: Minesweeper
games.description: The definitive browser Minesweeper: three difficulties, no-guess mode and global best times.
games.details: A clean, faithful implementation with an optional account for statistics and rankings. Keyboard and mouse fully supported.

games.name: Sudoku.com
games.description: Beautiful daily sudoku from Easybrain with hints, notes and every difficulty level.
games.details: The polished web version of the hugely popular mobile app. Free with ads; an optional premium removes them.
